sections.overview: Toxocara canis is a roundworm parasite of dogs and other canids.
sections.identification: Its thick-shelled eggs have a pitted surface.
sections.habitat: Adult worms live in the small intestine of dogs, especially young dogs.
sections.diet: The veterinary sources consulted do not separately describe what the adult worms consume in the host intestine.
sections.behavior: Eggs mature in soil; ingested larvae migrate through young dogs before adults settle in the intestine.
sections.reproduction: Adult females lay eggs in the intestine, and puppies may also acquire larvae before birth or through milk.
sections.ecology: Humans are accidental hosts; larvae may migrate through tissues but do not mature.
sections.conservation: The cited health sources give no conservation category for the parasite.
